```rust
//! A self‑contained, heavily commented implementation of a red‑black tree in Rust.
//! The code is intentionally verbose to aid understanding and is written in a
//! single file so it can be copied straight into a Rust project.
//!
//! Features:
//! - Node representation with color, key, value, and child/parent pointers.
//! - Full insertion with rebalancing (cases 1‑3 from CLRS).
//! - Full deletion with rebalancing (cases 1‑5 from CLRS).
//! - In‑order iterator that implements `Iterator`.
//! - `Debug` implementation that prints the tree in a readable format.
//! - A module of unit tests that exercise insertion, deletion, and invariants.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::fmt;
use std::rc::{Rc, Weak};

/// A convenient alias for a reference counted, mutable node.
type NodeRef<K, V> = Rc<RefCell<Node<K, V>>>;

/// The color of a node in a red‑black tree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Color {
    Red,
    Black,
}

/// Representation of a node in the tree.
/// The tree is generic over a key `K` and a value `V`.  The key must
/// implement `Ord` so that it can be compared to other keys.
struct Node<K, V> {
    key: K,
    value: V,
    color: Color,
    left: Option<NodeRef<K, V>>,
    right: Option<NodeRef<K, V>>,
    parent: Option<Weak<RefCell<Node<K, V>>>>,
}

impl<K, V> Node<K, V> {
    /// Create a new node that is initially red.
    fn new(key: K, value: V, parent: Option<Weak<RefCell<Node<K, V>>>>) -> NodeRef<K, V> {
        Rc::new(RefCell::new(Node {
            key,
            value,
            color: Color::Red,
            left: None,
            right: None,
            parent,
        }))
    }

    /// Helper to get the color of a node.  A `None` pointer is treated as black.
    fn color_of(node: &Option<NodeRef<K, V>>) -> Color {
        node.as_ref()
            .map(|n| n.borrow().color)
            .unwrap_or(Color::Black)
    }

    /// Helper to get the grandparent of a node.
    fn grandparent(node: &NodeRef<K, V>) -> Option<NodeRef<K, V>> {
        node.borrow()
            .parent
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|wp| wp.upgrade())
            .and_then(|p| p.borrow().parent.as_ref().and_then(|wp| wp.upgrade()))
    }

    /// Helper to get the sibling of a node.
    fn sibling(node: &NodeRef<K, V>) -> Option<NodeRef<K, V>> {
        let parent = node.borrow().parent.as_ref()?.upgrade()?;
        if Rc::ptr_eq(&parent.borrow().left.as_ref()?, node) {
            parent.borrow().right.clone()
        } else {
            parent.borrow().left.clone()
        }
    }

    /// Helper to get the uncle of a node.
    fn uncle(node: &NodeRef<K, V>) -> Option<NodeRef<K, V>> {
        Node::sibling(&node.borrow().parent.as_ref()?.upgrade()?)
    }

    /// Helper to get the other child of a node (the child that is not the given one).
    fn other_child(node: &NodeRef<K, V>, child: &NodeRef<K, V>) -> Option<NodeRef<K, V>> {
        if Rc::ptr_eq(&node.borrow().left.as_ref()?, child) {
            node.borrow().right.clone()
        } else {
            node.borrow().left.clone()
        }
    }
}

/// The main red‑black tree structure.
/// It contains a root pointer and a size counter.
pub struct RBTree<K, V> {
    root: Option<NodeRef<K, V>>,
    size: usize,
}

impl<K: Ord, V> RBTree<K, V> {
    /// Create an empty tree.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        RBTree { root: None, size: 0 }
    }

    /// Return the number of nodes in the tree.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    /// Check whether the tree is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.size == 0
    }

    /// Find a node with a given key.  Returns `None` if not found.
    pub fn get(&self, key: &K) -> Option<V>
    where
        V: Clone,
    {
        let mut node = self.root.clone();
        while let Some(n) = node {
            let n
